title: Mahua Moitra says BJP supporters attacked her convoy in Nadia; BJP calls it locals' protest
dek: The Trinamool MP says stones and eggs were thrown at her car in Kaliganj despite a High Court order on her security; a local BJP leader said only eggs were thrown, by people angered by her remarks.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra said a crowd of BJP supporters threw stones and eggs at her car and struck it with sticks in Kaliganj in Nadia district on Thursday morning, and accused the West Bengal Police of failing to stop them despite a Calcutta High Court order on her security. A local BJP leader described the protest as spontaneous anger among residents over remarks he attributed to her, and said only eggs had been thrown.

The incident took place in the Gobra gram panchayat area at about 11 am, as Moitra, the MP for Krishnanagar, travelled from Krishnanagar to Kaliganj, according to reports. Protesters surrounded her vehicle, waved black flags and BJP flags and shouted "go back" slogans, reports said. No injuries were reported. The police had not responded publicly to her allegations by Thursday evening.

## What each side says

Before the incident, Moitra posted on X that "80-90 BJP goons" were waiting at Gobra to attack her, and later that the police were "instead telling me to leave", according to reports. She said she had warned the police in advance, that the two constables accompanying her could not control the crowd, and accused the police of colluding with the protesters. "My safety under the order of Hon'ble HC Kolkata is your responsibility," she wrote. Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee asked whether the High Court would start contempt proceedings against the state government over the incident, reports said.

Sandipan Majumdar, media convener of the BJP's Nadia North organisational district, said the protest was a spontaneous expression of public anger over what he called Moitra's remarks about Hindu deities, and that nobody had thrown bombs at her, "only eggs", according to reports. The BJP's state leadership had not commented by Thursday evening. The BJP has governed West Bengal since May, with Suvendu Adhikari as Chief Minister.

## The court order

Moitra went to the Calcutta High Court on 21 September, alleging police inaction after protesters threw eggs at her and her car as she left a party meeting in Tehatta, also in Nadia, on 16 September. An interim order assigned two constables to accompany her for personal protection on visits to her constituency until 30 November, according to reports. Her plea for stronger security is pending before a Division Bench, which is next due to hear it on 27 November.

Moitra has represented Krishnanagar in the Lok Sabha since 2019 and is one of the Trinamool's most prominent voices in Parliament. Thursday's incident is the third of its kind she has reported this year. On 1 July she accused BJP workers of gathering outside her Krishnanagar office and throwing eggs; the BJP denied involvement in the earlier incidents.

## What happens next

The High Court's Division Bench is due to take up her security plea on 27 November, three days before the interim protection order expires. Moitra has not said whether she will file a police complaint or raise Thursday's incident in court before then.
